insight_to_chart_map.insight_summary: Month-to-month contracts are the epicenter of churn, accounting for nearly 90% of all lost customers.
insight_to_chart_map.chart_reasoning: This chart effectively shows two things at once: the absolute size of each customer segment (total bar height) and the absolute number of churners within it (colored segment). This combination makes it clear that the Month-to-Month segment is both large and has a severe churn problem, directly illustrating why it contributes so much to total churn. Adding a percentage annotation for the churn rate provides the final piece of necessary information in one view.

alternatives_rejected.reason_rejected: A pie chart showing the composition of churners would illustrate the '90% of churn' point, but would completely hide the underlying churn *rate*. It fails to show that the rate for Month-to-Month customers is 42.7% vs. just 2.7% for 2-year contracts, which is a critical part of the 'why'.

alternatives_rejected.chart: Two Separate Bar Charts (one for rates, one for counts)
alternatives_rejected.reason_rejected: While accurate, this approach increases the cognitive load on the stakeholder by forcing them to visually integrate two separate charts. A single, well-designed grouped bar chart conveys the same information more efficiently and has a stronger immediate impact.

insight_to_chart_map.insight_summary: The premium Fiber optic service has a critical retention problem, but providing Tech Support cuts this specific churn risk by more than half.
insight_to_chart_map.chart_reasoning: A grouped bar chart is the standard and most effective way to visualize an interaction effect between two categorical variables. By placing Internet Service on the x-axis and grouping the bars by Tech Support status, the chart directly invites the comparison that is the core of the insight: the churn reduction from having Tech Support is visually much larger for Fiber optic than for DSL customers.

alternatives_rejected.reason_rejected: A slope chart could connect 'No Tech Support' to 'Yes Tech Support' with lines for Fiber and DSL. While good for showing change, with only two points on the x-axis, the comparison of the magnitude of the rates (the bar heights) is often clearer and more intuitive for a business audience in a bar chart format.

Displaying four separate numbers (e.g., Fiber with Support: 20.0% churn) would be factually correct but visually inert. It would force the audience to perform mental calculations to grasp the insight. The purpose of a chart is to make the comparison and the pattern instantly obvious, which a grouped bar chart achieves.

insight_to_chart_map.insight_summary: Customers paying with non-automatic methods churn at a much higher rate, with the Electronic check process being particularly problematic (45.3% churn).
insight_to_chart_map.chart_reasoning: This chart is optimal for several reasons. First, a bar chart is the best choice for comparing rates across categories. Second, making it horizontal gracefully handles the long labels of the payment methods without rotation. Third, sorting the bars by churn rate from highest to lowest immediately draws attention to the main offender ('Electronic check'), making the key insight instantly visible.

alternatives_rejected.reason_rejected: The long category labels for payment methods would need to be rotated or truncated on a vertical axis, which harms readability. A horizontal layout is superior for long categorical labels.

A pie chart is inappropriate here. We are comparing rates between distinct categories, not showing a part-to-whole composition. A pie chart would fail to communicate the key message that the churn rate for one category is over 2.5 times higher than others.

dashboard_architecture.interactivity_spec: The dashboard should support basic cross-filtering. When a user clicks on a segment in one chart (e.g., the 'Month-to-month' category in the contract chart), all other charts on the dashboard should filter to show data for only that selected segment. This allows for simple, intuitive drill-down without needing complex filter panes.

anti_pattern_audit.correction_applied: Ensured the Y-axis (or X-axis for horizontal bars) for all charts showing rates or counts starts at zero. This prevents the misleading exaggeration of differences between categories.

anti_pattern_audit.anti_pattern_found: Chart title states category, not insight (potential risk)
anti_pattern_audit.correction_applied: Chart titles were written as declarative headlines that state the key finding (e.g., 'Month-to-Month Contracts Drive 89% of Churn' instead of 'Churn by Contract Type'). This helps the executive audience grasp the main point immediately.

anti_pattern_audit.anti_pattern_found: Using Pie Chart with 4 slices for PaymentMethod (potential risk)
anti_pattern_audit.correction_applied: A pie chart for the 'PaymentMethod' insight was considered and rejected. A sorted bar chart was chosen instead because it is far more effective at showing the relative magnitude of the churn rates, which is the core insight, whereas a pie chart is for part-to-whole comparisons.

accessibility_review.notes: All chart specifications use color-blind safe palettes (e.g., blue/orange, sequential blues) and rely on position and labels, not just color, to convey information. Font sizes are specified to be >= 12pt for labels and 16pt+ for titles. Descriptive alt text has been written for each visualization. Contrast ratios for text and background will need to be checked in the final tool but are assumed to meet WCAG AA standards in this design.

narrative_flow.hook: The dashboard opens with the most critical number: the 26.5% overall churn rate. The eye is then drawn to the largest chart, 'Month-to-Month Contracts Drive 89% of Churn', immediately presenting the biggest part of the problem and the primary antagonist of our story.
context_sequence: After seeing *who* is churning (M2M customers), the user explores *why*. The 'Tech Support Halves Churn for High-Risk Fiber Customers' chart reveals a service quality issue with the premium product, providing a more nuanced driver.
Next, the 'Electronic Check Payments' chart adds another layer, showing that operational friction in processes like payments is also a significant contributor to churn.
narrative_flow.payoff: The narrative concludes in the 'Key Recommendations' text box, which synthesizes the evidence from the charts into actionable advice: '1. Launch a campaign to migrate high-value M2M customers to 1-year contracts. 2. Bundle Tech Support with all Fiber optic plans to fix the leaky premium bucket.' This provides a clear resolution and path forward for the stakeholder.

chart_titles_as_insight_headlines: Tech Support Halves Churn for High-Risk Fiber Customers
Electronic Check Payments Have 2.5x Higher Churn
phase_8_handoff.narrative_arc_summary: The story begins by identifying the 'villain': Month-to-Month contracts are responsible for almost all churn. We then uncover its accomplices: poor service experience for Fiber customers and high friction in the payment process. The story resolves with a clear set of targeted interventions to fight these specific problems, empowering leadership to take decisive action.
